message.content: {"name":"end_turn","parameters":{"public_message":"Passing.","private_thought":"1v1. Cash $1261 on CT (9) after $600 light-blue hotel. Next roll (11-21) is mine or mortgaged \u2014 no rent. PP is 28 away, BW 30, GO 31, so dark blues are before GO and not this roll; earliest hit is my 3rd move. $1261 covers neither PP ($1500, short $239) nor BW ($2000, short $739). Do not pre-sell: a hotel is only $50 and I can liquidate on the hit. PP is survivable (strip one pink for $250, keep two hotels). BW forces near-total pink liquidation ($750) and likely a loss \u2014 selling now does not fix that unless I gut the only weapon. p1 is on PRR with $1366; pinks are ~36 away so they pass GO first. One pink is payable; two can be absorbed via light-blue/brown sales (~$625) without touching dark blues; a third still forces a dark-blue downgrade. Do not unmortgage PRR/TN (\u2212EV, no set, cuts cushion). Do not trade TN (completes oranges), cash (funds reds/yellows/greens), or GOOJFs. They will not break PP/BW. Keep both GOOJF \u2014 Go to Jail (21 away) is before PP, so jail-stay may skip dark blues. End turn."}}
message.reasoning:
I need to make a decision in Monopoly.

I am p2. I paid $600 rent to p1 on CONNECTICUT_AVENUE and now have $1261 cash. I own a pink monopoly with hotels on ST_CHARLES_PLACE, STATES_AVENUE, and VIRGINIA_AVENUE. PENNSYLVANIA_RAILROAD and TENNESSEE_AVENUE are mortgaged. I have two get-out-of-jail cards. The opponent has $1366.

The opponent owns hotels on most of the board. Oranges are split between us. They have St James and New York mortgaged. I have Tennessee mortgaged. They own almost everything else.

I am on space 9 (CONNECTICUT_AVENUE). The opponent is on space 15 (PENNSYLVANIA_RAILROAD).

A roll from CONNECTICUT_AVENUE cannot land on the dark blue hotels. The closest dark blues are 28 spaces away. The next roll would hit my own properties or other spaces. I have enough cash to cover a $1500 rent on Park Place.

I am short $239 for Park Place and $739 for Boardwalk. I will not sell hotels or unmortgage the railroads and Tennessee. Trading Tennessee would complete the opponent's orange set. I will not give cash or get-out-of-jail cards. I will keep the pink hotels to pressure the opponent into downgrading their dark blues.

The opponent is on PENNSYLVANIA_RAILROAD. Their pink hotels are behind them at ST_CHARLES_PLACE, STATES_AVENUE, and VIRGINIA_AVENUE. They must travel 36 spaces to reach them, passing GO first. From their current position, the next roll would land on Community Chest, my mortgaged TENNESSEE_AVENUE, New York, Free Parking, Kentucky, Chance, Indiana, Illinois, or B&O.

The opponent's next roll would hit Atlantic and Ventnor. I still need cash before reaching the dark blues. Selling the pink hotels could raise funds, since hotel sales return half the purchase price.

Selling a pink hotel for $50 would drop rent by $125 or $150. That is too steep. I will not sell hotels.

Unmortgaging the railroads costs $110 and $99 respectively. The return is only $25 in rent, so it is negative expected value. I will consider trading with p1 to raise cash.

Tennessee would complete the opponent's orange monopoly, which is too dangerous to trade. The get-out-of-jail cards are not worth trading for cash. Staying in jail could avoid the dark blues, but it would also prevent the opponent from landing on my pink hotels.

I am not in jail. I will keep my get-out-of-jail cards for myself. Selling buildings to raise cash is impractical because hotel sales return only $50 each. A full pink strip plus one house covers Boardwalk rent.

Selling one pink hotel returns $50 plus four houses, totaling $250. That is only a quarter of the Boardwalk shortfall. A full pink strip would raise $750 but drop rent to the base doubled amount, which is still too low.

Three full pink strips would raise $750 but destroy the hotels and weaken the pink set. That is too risky.

I am on space 9. The next roll lands between spaces 11 and 21. From there I cannot reach GO before hitting dark blues.

Turn B lands on spaces 13 through 33. From there I can reach GO, Park Place, or Boardwalk on turn C. The worst case is landing on 33 and missing both dark blues without passing GO first.

I cannot pass GO before hitting the dark blues. After two rolls I am still 16 to 26 spaces from Park Place and 18 to 30 from Boardwalk. On the third roll I can reach either dark blue or GO. The opponent must travel almost a full circle to reach my pink hotels, so they will not land on them before I hit the dark blues.

The opponent will pass GO first and collect $200. They will land on my pink hotels around turn C. I must survive the dark blues on that same turn. Selling one full pink strip now would raise cash to $1511 and cover Park Place with $11 left over. Two full strips would raise cash to $1761 and cover both dark blues with $261 left over. Three full strips would raise cash to $2011.

Selling all three hotels would raise cash to $2011, but I would have no hotels left. The pink set would drop to base doubled rent of roughly $20 and $24, which is too weak to pressure the opponent.

Selling only the hotels while keeping four houses each would raise about $150, leaving me short by $89 for Park Place and $589 for Boardwalk. The four-house rent would still be $625, $625, and $750, which remains very painful.

I must check whether the game requires selling houses evenly. Selling two houses alongside the hotels would raise $250, covering Park Place with $11 left over, but that still leaves a $739 shortfall for Boardwalk.

Pre-selling buildings now would reduce rent pressure before the opponent might land on them. It is better to wait until I actually land on a dark blue and sell only then. The probability of hitting Boardwalk or Park Place before passing GO from my current position is low.

I am calculating the exact probability of landing on Park Place or Boardwalk within three rolls. The sum of three 2d6 rolls ranges from 6 to 36 with a mean of 21, so reaching exactly 28 is unlikely. I need to determine whether this occurs before passing GO.

I am now calculating the exact probability of landing on Park Place or Boardwalk within three rolls. The sum of three 2d6 rolls ranges from 6 to 36, so a roll of 28 lands on Park Place, 30 on Boardwalk, and 29 hits the Luxury Tax between them. A roll of 31 or higher passes GO, while anything below 27 leaves me still short of the dark blues, meaning I could hit them on turn four instead.

The normal approximation for a 6d6 sum of 28 yielded roughly 5.9%, which seems too high for a discrete point. I am now looking up the exact known probability for that sum.

I am checking whether the opponent can land on my pink hotels before I reach the dark blues. If they do, keeping my hotels may force them to sell their dark blue hotels and save me money.

The opponent is on space 15. They must travel 36 spaces to reach my pink hotels, so they will pass GO first and land on my pinks around turn five. I need about four turns to reach the dark blues, so I will likely face their dark blue rent before they can land on my pinks.

The turn sequence is p1, then me, then p1, then me. After this post-turn, p1 moves first, then I move, and so on. I will likely reach the dark blues on my third movement, while p1 has only moved twice.

I will likely pay dark blue rent before collecting from the opponent. I have $1261 in cash. Landing on Park Place would leave a $239 shortfall, and landing on Boardwalk would leave a $739 shortfall. I am calculating whether selling all three hotels at debt time can raise enough money while still threatening rent.

Liquidating all three hotels would raise $750, giving me $2011 after Boardwalk. That leaves the pink set bare with only $11 cash and no hotels. The opponent still holds hotels on dark blues, light blues, and browns, so a next rent of over $250 would bankrupt me unless I mortgage my unmortgaged pinks for about $220.

Full liquidation after Boardwalk leaves only $231, which is too little to survive a light blue hotel rent. If I land on Park Place instead, selling one hotel and four houses raises $250, covering the $1500 cost with $11 left over while keeping two hotels intact.

Partial liquidation after Park Place leaves two hotels intact, so the opponent would face a costly demolition. Boardwalk would require near-total liquidation and likely lose the game. The key is avoiding Boardwalk or having another plan. I may hit a Chance card before reaching the dark blues.

The Chance card at space 22 is reachable by turn two, while the one at space 36 is near the same time as Park Place. An Advance to Boardwalk card would be catastrophic if I lack cash. I am now considering preemptively raising cash or trading with p1 for Tennessee Avenue, which would complete an orange monopoly.

I should not trade Tennessee Avenue. The opponent has $1366, but fully hoteling the orange set would cost about $1500. They could only build roughly eleven houses, yet that is still extremely dangerous. A Get Out of Jail Free card is worth only fifty to one hundred dollars and is not worth the risk.

I am now considering buying a property from the opponent to break their dangerous monopolies. Destroying the dark blue set would remove their kill shot, but they would never sell Park Place or Boardwalk for $1261. The light blue hotels are similarly expensive to acquire. The brown hotels are less threatening.

The opponent could unmortgage their red properties for roughly four hundred dollars and build hotels there, which would be extremely dangerous. They have not done so, likely because they are saving cash to pay my pink rents or because the game rules prevent building while mortgaged.

I will not trade cash to the opponent, since that would let them build red, yellow, or green hotels. Buying a mortgaged red property to break its monopoly is unlikely to succeed at a fair price, and I need every dollar for survival. I have two Get Out of Jail Free cards.

Go to Jail is at space 30, twenty-one spaces from my current position. That is closer than Park Place at 28. Landing exactly on the Jail square would send me to jail and skip the dark blues entirely. This could be a useful escape.

I cannot choose to go to jail now. The best post-turn action is end_turn. Trading for dark blue properties would waste an exchange.

I considered trading for Boardwalk or a light blue hotel, but the opponent would never accept such offers. Proposing a trade is not clearly better than ending the turn, and it wastes one of my twenty available exchanges.

Unmortgaging properties would cost money and reduce my survival cushion. I will not sell buildings now; the liquidate-if-hit strategy is still the right approach. My cash balance of $1261 after paying the $600 rent on Connecticut Avenue matches the earlier projection.

The shortfall for Park Place is now $239 and Boardwalk $739. Pre-selling a hotel would only raise about $50 and weaken the threat. Selling one full pink strip would cover the rent but leave me with just one hotel. Waiting to land on Park Place is preferable because it preserves the hotel if I avoid that space.

Pre-selling a hotel for cash would reduce the opponent's busting chance, but waiting is still the better strategy. Selling one pink strip would not cover Boardwalk rent, and liquidating almost everything would lose the game regardless of whether I land there. The best action remains ending the turn.

I will keep my public message brief and avoid telegraphing weakness. I am updating my private notes for future reference.

I also calculated the opponent's cash flow after paying a pink hotel rent. If they pay $750, they would have $616 left. If they pay $900, they would have $466 left. A second hotel payment of $750 would leave them $284 short, forcing them to sell buildings.

The opponent's cash balance increased to $1366 after I paid the $600 rent. A single pink hotel rent is now easily payable, and a second hit is also manageable. Selling dark blue hotels would raise only about half their cost, so they could likely survive both pink hits without selling buildings.

Liquidating all light blue and brown houses would raise roughly $625, bringing the opponent's total to about $1991. That is enough to cover both pink hotel hits without selling any dark blue hotels.

The opponent can now absorb two pink hotel hits by liquidating light blue and brown houses, leaving dark blue hotels intact. A third pink hit would force a dark blue downgrade, so the opponent would survive all three pink hits without selling any dark blue hotels. This weakens my position because I must now hit pinks three times before they go bankrupt to my hotels.
